About

Analytics with a business head and a conscience.

I'm a recent MSc Business Analytics graduate (Trinity College Dublin) with a Computer Science degree behind it. I work end-to-end: pulling data together, building the model or dashboard, and sitting with stakeholders to make sure it answers the question they actually asked.

My comfort zone is SQL, Python, Tableau and Power BI, plus the data-engineering and governance layers that make analytics trustworthy — fairness audits, explainability, and GDPR-compliant design. I care as much about whether a number can be trusted as about what it says.

Selected work

Projects

MSc Dissertation · Trinity Business School

Academic Pre-Evaluation Dashboard

The problemAdmissions reviewers needed to score applicants consistently and fairly, and to see why a candidate scored the way they did — not just trust a number.
What I builtA six-part scoring model (GPA normalisation, quantitative readiness, subject breadth, prerequisites, recency) using scikit-learn, XGBoost and Bayesian logistic regression, validated on synthetic data for 300–500 applicants across 8–10 countries. Wrapped in a Streamlit dashboard with SHAP explanations, plus a fairness audit across country, institution type and gender and a GDPR Article 22 audit trail with logged overrides.
Explainable, audited scoring · 12-week build with the live admissions team

MSc Business Analytics · Trinity College Dublin · Solution design

HelloFresh AI Demand Forecasting & Menu Optimisation

The briefDesign an AI solution to cut ingredient waste, lift customer retention and reduce fulfilment cost across a global meal-kit business's value chain.
What I designedAn end-to-end AI system: five models selected with rationale (XGBoost + LSTM demand forecasting, Neural Collaborative Filtering for menu recommendations, Random Forest churn, Isolation Forest spoilage anomaly, LightGBM labour optimisation); the data pipeline from Kafka ingestion through Snowflake, dbt and Airflow to model services and activation; plus a KPI framework, a 12-month phased rollout, a risk register, and GDPR Article 22 governance with human-in-the-loop overrides.
Design targets: 65% → 80% retention · −20% ingredient waste · −15% fulfilment cost · <8% forecast MAPE

B.Tech Capstone · SRM · Built & benchmarked

Predictive Maintenance with IoT & Machine Learning

The problemIn ice manufacturing, gas-pressure spikes in shell-and-tube heat exchangers are a safety hazard. The goal: predict abnormal conditions from live sensor data early enough to prevent accidents.
What I builtAn end-to-end IoT + ML system. An Arduino UNO and ESP32 with temperature and humidity sensors stream live readings to the cloud (Firebase); an SVM classifier trained on that data flags abnormal conditions, and the Blynk app raises real-time alerts. I benchmarked the SVM against Random Forest, ANN, RNN and KNN on accuracy, precision, recall and F1.
SVM gave the best accuracy (97.5%) and precision of the five models · low recall identified as the key limitation to fix
